summary: Phase 1 Website Claims Correction passes security/anti-pattern review. All 20/20 phase-w3-claims tests pass, lint and check-types are clean, and no secrets, credentials, or auth bypasses were introduced in the locale/metadata changes. The A2 consent-blind-publish gate is exercised by the helper audit (missingConsentCount === 0 because all case studies are relabeled illustrative/placeholder). A latent key-mismatch in the test's consentIndex builder vs. the helper's claim-text lookup is noted as non-blocking. Plan truthfulness (A5) was corrected from 19/19 to 20/20 and the missing CodeCamp/Science metadata + b2b-solutions badge changes were documented. No registry overstatement (A6) or over-broad literal filters (A7) were found.
nonblocking_findings: A2 latent key mismatch: phase-w3-claims.test.ts buildConsentIndex() keys consent proof by filename-derived subject (e.g. 'school-a'), while product-claim-helper.audit() looks up consent by the full claim.text. For a future published-case-study claim, a consent file named by subject will fail closed (missingConsentCount > 0) because the keys do not match. This is not a bypass but a usability issue to resolve when real case studies are reintroduced.

A7 narrow regex: Group 1G's '3x faster' scanner uses only the Unicode multiplication sign (/3×/g). An ASCII variant ('3x faster', '3X faster') would not be caught. The claim is currently removed, so risk is low.
